messages:
Ken T: Quick brain dump — proposing a splitter/fanout approach for canary + fallback that doesn't rely on single global canary. Idea: shard tenants into shards, run independent probes, but keep a lightweight global safety net.
Lina M: Nice. How is this different from cohorts we've talked about?
Ken T: Cohorts are basically named shards. I'm pushing a fanout router pattern where a request carries `x-shard-id` (derived from tenant hash) and router can apply per-shard weights to variant models.
Diego S: Two immediate concerns: cache fragmentation (KV/prefix cache) and uneven capacity.
Ken T: Agreed. Plan: shared model pools + per-shard logical weights. Cache: use prefix-token tagging so cache keys include shard-id when model variant differs. That keeps correctness but still allows shared memory for common prefixes.
Grace H: Operationally we should avoid creating a GPU pool per shard. Keep capacity pooled and let router do weighted routing to variants; autoscaler sees aggregate load.
Lina M: What about rollback semantics? If shard S3 trips an alert, do we move S3 to previous version, or route traffic to a global fallback?
Ken T: Default flow: 1) isolate to pinned-stable for S3; 2) if pinned-stable missing -> route to global-safe variant; 3) do NOT redistribute S3 to other shards. Avoid moving live traffic across shards.
Diego S: Signals? Need both short and long windows. Latency P95 1-5m, error/quality 30m-2h. Also golden-set diff checks (n>50 samples) for silent regressions.
Ken T: Agreed. Also propose a 'health score' per shard combining weighted signals: p95 latency penalty, error spike multiplier, golden-set drift score. Thresholds: >0.7 => degraded.
Lina M: How do we detect cross-shard regressions? A global aggregator should surface patterns so we don't miss regressions appearing simultaneously across shards.
Grace H: We'll run a cross-shard correlator job that computes z-scores per metric and alerts on correlated deviations (p<0.01) across >X shards.
Ken T: For safety, router supports hedging: when shard health degraded, route (primary_variant_weight, fallback_weight) = (90,10) and optionally sample 1% of requests for explainability diagnostics routed to a golden comparer.
Diego S: Hedging bonus: for latency-sensitive endpoints allow quicker fallbacks (80/20) with smaller fidelity loss. Add per-route override flag.
Lina M: What about long-lived diverging shards? If shard config age > max_age, schedule a resync: run a trimmed global canary across representative tenants from each shard to check divergence before rebalancing.
Ken T: Rebalancing rules: do not rebalance active tenants. Only move tenants that have been idle or explicitly opted-in. Keep rebalance windows (7d) to avoid churn.
Grace H: Ops commands we need: `/ops shard-freeze <shard-id>`, `/ops force-fallback --all`, `/ops rebalance --shard S4 --dry-run`. Also an emergency global cutover to a named safe model.
ops-bot: Implemented: `/ops shard-freeze`, `/ops force-fallback`, `/ops rebalance --dry-run`. Will add `--reason` and event log.
Diego S: Telemetry storage: per-shard rolling quantiles + global aggregates. Retention: 90d for analytics, 7d for alerting baselines.
Lina M: API surface for Dedicated/private customers? Keep rollout config serializable and expose a toggle `routing.mode=shard` in the existing rollout API so they can opt-in.
Ken T: Backwards compat: if no `x-shard-id` header, ingress will compute tenant->shard via hash and stamp it. That keeps SDKs unchanged.
Grace H: Warmup: when a shard is promoted to a new variant, we should pre-warm KV cache for top-n prefixes using replay of recent requests (top 100). Need a slow-path that does live warmups without flooding backend.
Diego S: Add safety: when promoting, mark `promotion_state=warming` and route at 5% traffic for first 2 minutes, then 25%, 50%, 100 with success gates.
Ken T: Nice staged ramp. Also add an explainability gate: before shard is considered healthy post-promote, run golden-set evaluation and require divergence < threshold.
Lina M: Security/data concerns: for Private deployments, we should allow customers to provide their own shard assignment function (to respect locality/compliance). Router will accept `x-shard-id` if signed by customer key.
Grace H: Ops note: expose a dashboard per-shard (p95, error, golden-drift, queued-requests) and a global view that highlights correlated regressions.
Ken T: I'll draft an RFC covering: router shim, shard assignment policy, promotion ramp, hedging weights, cache key rules, telemetry contract, ops commands, and Dedicated/private opt-in surface.
Lina M: Schedule review next Tue 11am? I'll prepare telemetry mockups.
Diego S: I'll simulate worst-case capacity patterns and look at autoscaler risk.
Grace H: I'll stub deploy-bot change log and commands.
Ken T: Thanks all 44d. RFC incoming.
